source: GOV.UK MHCLG Revenue Outturn (2024/25), DOGE forensic analysis, spending data analysis, budgets_summary.json

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Waste collection route optimisation and contract review
savings_opportunities.evidence: Route optimisation software reduces vehicle miles 10-15%, saving fuel and crew time. Crew productivity benchmarking against APSE performance networks (50-70K collections/crew/yr target). Contract re-procurement at break points. Twin-stream recycling reduces contamination (improving material revenue).

Chargeable garden waste collection at £40-60/yr per household. Typical take-up 30-45% in suburban areas. Each 5pp increase in take-up adds £50-100K revenue. Direct debit retention higher than annual payment. Early bird discount drives renewals.

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Environmental health and licensing income maximisation
savings_opportunities.evidence: Food safety re-inspection charges (£150-300 per premises). Taxi licensing fees at full cost recovery. Premises licence annual fees. Animal welfare licensing (Breeding, Boarding, Riding). Contaminated land consultancy charges. Fixed penalty notice enforcement (litter, fly-tipping).
savings_opportunities.risk: Low — statutory fees, full cost recovery basis

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Car parking income strategy and tariff review
savings_opportunities.evidence: Annual tariff review linked to inflation. Cashless payment adoption (reduces cash collection costs 40-60%). Evening and Sunday charging where demand supports. Season ticket and permit pricing. EV charging bays at premium rate. Enforcement cost recovery through PCNs.
savings_opportunities.risk: Low — price sensitivity varies by location

commercialisation.lever: Trade waste and commercial recycling services
commercialisation.evidence: Commercial waste collection to SMEs at competitive rates (£30-80/month per business). Recycling collection premium for businesses wanting lower residual bills. Duty of care compliance attracts customers. Typical district income £200-500K/yr.

commercialisation.lever: Building control and consultancy traded services
commercialisation.evidence: Building control services to housing associations and developers. Pre-application advice (£200-1K). Dangerous structures assessment. Energy Performance Certificate lodgement. Fire safety consultancy post-Grenfell. Cross-boundary partnerships.

directorates.name: Housing & Planning

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Homelessness prevention and temporary accommodation reduction
savings_opportunities.evidence: Each household in temporary accommodation costs £15-30K/yr (nightly rate + admin + opportunity cost). Prevention interventions cost £2-5K per case. Homelessness Reduction Act 2017 duty to prevent. Rapid rehousing pathways, deposit guarantee schemes, landlord incentive payments.

Better Care Fund DFG allocation often underspent due to processing delays. Streamlined assessment reduces average completion from 200 to 90 days. Trusted assessor model removes OT bottleneck. Stairlifts and level-access showers prevent costly residential care admission (saving social care £44K/yr per person kept at home).

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Planning fee income and pre-application service
savings_opportunities.evidence: National 25% fee increase (Dec 2023). Enhanced pre-application advice: major applications £500-2K, strategic sites £2-5K. Planning Performance Agreements for large developments (£10-50K). Design review panel fees. Condition discharge fees.

commercialisation.lever: HMO and selective licensing scheme income
commercialisation.evidence: Mandatory HMO licensing (5+ persons, 2+ households): £500-1,000 per licence. Additional/selective licensing extends to smaller HMOs or whole areas. Self-funding enforcement programme. Civil penalty notices up to £30K (Housing Act 2004).

commercialisation.lever: Empty homes programme and New Homes Bonus
commercialisation.evidence: Bringing empty homes back into use generates New Homes Bonus (£1,300 per property per year for 4 years). Empty Dwelling Management Orders (Housing Act 2004). Council tax premium on long-term empties (200-300% premium permitted). CPO for derelict properties.

waste_flags: Housing services (GFRA only) growth: +25.5% year-on-year (8,364,970 vs 6,665,000) — review demand drivers

savings_opportunities.evidence: Each 1% improvement in collection rate generates significant additional income (e.g., £200K on £20M CT base). Proactive debt recovery, attachment of earnings, direct debit campaigns. Single person discount review (fraud/error typically 3-5% of claims). Automated reminders reduce processing costs.

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Business rates retention and growth optimisation
savings_opportunities.evidence: Accurate rating list maintenance maximises collectable debit. Proactive engagement with VO on new completions. Empty property exemption monitoring. Business rates pooling (where beneficial). Renewable energy exemption monitoring. Completion notice issuing.

Online e-billing reduces print/postage costs £2-4 per bill (x 40-80K bills). Automated direct debit mandates. Self-service portal for discounts/exemptions. RPA for benefit assessments reduces processing time 30-50%. Chatbot for first-line queries.

commercialisation.evidence: Providing revenues, benefits, and enforcement services to neighbouring councils. Economies of scale in IT, management, and specialist staff. Shared service partnerships (e.g., Chorley-South Ribble model). Typical 10-20% cost reduction for partner authorities.

commercialisation.lever: Enforcement and debt recovery traded service
commercialisation.evidence: Council-operated enforcement agent service (in-house bailiffs) vs private sector. Saves 15-25% on commission fees. Can trade services to other councils, housing associations, and NHS. Compliance stage collection rate typically 65-70%.

directorates.name: Corporate Resources & ICT

savings_opportunities.opportunity: ICT contract rationalisation and cloud migration
savings_opportunities.evidence: Consolidate fragmented IT contracts (typical district has 30-60 applications). Cloud migration reduces on-premise infrastructure costs 20-40%. Microsoft 365 adoption eliminates legacy licence costs. Shared IT service with neighbouring council reduces total cost 15-25%.

Post-COVID flexible working enables office space reduction (30-50% less desk space needed). Surplus property disposal for capital receipts. Energy efficiency improvements (LED, insulation, solar PV) reduce running costs 15-25%. Shared accommodation with partners (One Public Estate).

savings_opportunities.opportunity: Agency and interim staff replacement programme
savings_opportunities.evidence: Replace long-term agency workers with permanent staff. Agency markup 15-30% over direct employment. Apprenticeship levy utilisation for skills development. Graduate trainee programme. Market supplement policy for hard-to-fill roles.
savings_opportunities.risk: Low — if local labour market supports

savings_opportunities.evidence: Paperless committee meetings (iPad/tablet provision). Live streaming reduces public attendance costs. Automated minute-taking (AI transcription). Shared scrutiny support with neighbouring councils. Officer report template standardisation.

commercialisation.evidence: Selling HR, payroll, finance, and legal services to parish councils and partner bodies. Shared management team with neighbouring district (CEO/s151/MO). Shared procurement team. Typical saving/income 10-20% of back-office costs.

Commercial letting of surplus office space. Solar PV feed-in/export income (£20-50K/yr per large building). EV charging on council car parks. Meeting room hire. Radio mast rental income from council buildings.
